title: The Inclusion of Gentiles and the Protection of New Believers
english: And they hunger and thirst according to the present life, and [He] gives eternal food to those being distressed, according to the Beatitudes: 'Blessed are those who hunger and thirst for righteousness, for they shall themselves be filled' (Matt 5:6), and according to the prophetic word saying, 'Behold, my servants shall eat, but you shall hunger' (Isa 55:20).

If one wishes to perceive these things sensorially: He gave manna to those hungering in the wilderness, and nourished five thousand hungry men; and He gave also to Elijah and Daniel, the one through ravens, the other through the prophet Ambakum. And He made judgment for those being wronged: Joseph by the Egyptians, Susanna by the judges of Israel, and David being wronged by Saul and others more; the Scripture is most full of these. (Gen 42:21; Dan 13)

Those being broken are the same as those being laid low, differing only in thought; for they are hindered from acting and from running toward the truth, being laid low by wickedness, they fall from the height of virtue and happen to be broken. It must be said that those laid low and broken are those sinning in practice, being blind ones who cast away the seeing of the intellect, so that they do not see the beauties of the dogmas of the truth.

Just as he released the laid low and straightened the broken, desiring the forgiveness of sins, so he enlightened the blind, having enlightened the eyes of their hearts, he himself about whom Paul writes: 'The God who said, Let light shine out of darkness, has shone in your hearts to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God' (2 Cor 4:6).

Since the word spoken refers to the memory of the righteous among the converts: those loved by the Lord are called righteous, those having been pleasing to him according to the Old Scripture; but converts are those called from the Gentiles upon the teaching of the Gospel. And what the intellect questions, it is to be heard from the Savior saying, 'Many prophets and righteous men desired to see what you see and to hear what you hear' (Matt 23:37). Among these righteous ones is Abraham, concerning whom it is written: 'Abraham believed God, and it was counted to him for righteousness' (Gen 15:6). And concerning the Gentiles as being converts, it is to be heard from Paul saying, 'Therefore remember...'

You used to be of the Gentiles, and once you were separated from the commonwealth of Israel (Eph 2:12). But now, you who once became distant, have become near in the eye of our Lord Jesus Christ; for He is our peace. Furthermore, you are no longer strangers and sojourners, but fellow citizens with the saints and members of the household of God (Eph 2:19), having been built up upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets (Eph 2:20).

Concerning these proselytes, Moses said to Israel, saying, 'If you do not obey the commandments of the Lord your God, the proselyte who is among you will be above you, but you will be below' (Deut 23:7), through the changing of circumstances. Indeed, before the coming of the Savior, those of the Gentiles who hurried to worship God approached Israel being instructed and obeying them; but now, those who wish to approach the faith of Christ from the Israelites are setting aside the evangelical commonwealth, approaching as sacrifices among those of the Gentiles who have believed.

In addition to this, take care lest the proselytes who are coming now through godliness—though those who have passed through and been perfected in it are called righteous—should be lost; for God loves the righteous, but He guards the proselytes. For those who have arrived immediately by the word of truth, lest they may not be strong and firm, need the guarding of the Lord so that they may remain unhurt, whereas the righteous are made members of Him and loved by Him through perfection.

He will take up the orphan and the widow (Ps 68:5)—not any widows, but those continuing in purity and reverence. Such is Anna, the daughter of Phanuel, whom the Gospel remembers (Luke 2:36). The Lord will take up such a widow through incorruptible prudence, along with her well-endured orphanhood, lifting them up and raising them by virtue, so that He may also lead them into the heavenly blessings.

It is possible to say of orphans being taken up that they are the godly who leave behind parents; such as Abraham, going out from the land and kindred and the house of his father at God's calling of him (Gen 12:1); and also James and John, having left Zebedee their father through the invitation of Jesus (Mark 1:19). title: Allegorical Interpretation of Psalm 146/147
english: You say that widows are being taken after having been separated from men in perfect prudence, by the mutual consent of both, the man and the woman, for the same purpose as those who dissolved the marriage. But more allegorically, the souls that cast off the one who became their father, the devil, are orphans and widows being taken. Once these are taken, the way of the sinners, which is nothing other than wickedness, shall be destroyed by God (Ps 145:10).

Zion, the watchful and examining one of the truth, is the perfect soul, the church of the living God; your God shall reign forever (Ps 146:3), the end of the kingdom shall not be delayed, his rule extending from generation to generation. It is said in this psalm before this, concerning his unending kingdom extending through all ages and how he rules from generation to generation. Therefore, being satisfied with those, as they apply them also to the present words, we shall say nothing more.

Since the psalm is good and beneficial to the user, praising its honor, announce to him that in praising this psalm, there is no difference from that one, especially since the one singing in spirit and mind and singing with the heart does not differ. If, however, to sing signifies to act in practice, it is advised to those who have perfected this good psalm to also praise Christ through theology, so that, having been perfected in practice and thought, they may rejoice in God; for he says, 'A sacrifice of praise shall glorify me' (Ps 146:5), and the Spirit commands to bring it forward, as those who say, 'Offer to God a sacrifice of praise.'

He also takes up the meek (Ps 147:6), lifting them up to where they inherit the land. But that land they inherit is high above. Therefore it has also been written, 'He will bring you up upon the good things of the earth,' and 'He will lift you up to inherit the land.' He takes up the meek, but he humbles the sinners as those who carry the image of the earth, thinking of low things and those upon the earth. Just as Paul, the meek one, was taken up to the third heaven (2 Cor 12:2) and to be a participant in unutterable things as if in paradise. And all those who call upon their names upon their lands, being in the flesh and not having the Spirit of God, having departed from God upon the earth, are written [down].

For thanksgiving, awakening those who have received so many good things. 'Begin,' he says, 'in confession, hymning and glorifying him for those things on which he worked' (Ps 146:8-9). And allegorically, his divine word surrounds the heaven with noetic clouds pouring down a noetic rain: for the heaven above rejoiced, and the clouds (surrounding him) rained down righteousness. From these noetic clouds he prepares rain for the earth, which Jesus spiritually sowed to bring forth fruit divided into one hundred and sixty and thirty, bringing up grass in the deserts for the great-souled and providing for the soul a fresh green clover to be found upon the slavery of men to be fed as food.

But the slavery of men is the irrational animals. This is said concerning the things destined, as we saw in the hundred and third Psalm; let us see them further. He brings up and gives food to the simpler sheep and cattle of those having believed in Christ, which are being saved apart from men. But he gives food not only to these, but also to the high-flying ones, for he commanded the young ravens to call upon him. God gives food to these, since they call upon him, according to the perfect men, concerning whom it is said, 'They called upon the Lord, and he heard them' (Ps 145:4). And you will understand the young ravens to be those from the nations who have believed and because of this call upon the Lord, so that he may give them spiritual food. For the raven is unclean and gloomy. Such are the evil demons and those who have added to impiety, of whom they were formerly sons, but having believed they obtained the heavenly food.

The gates of Jerusalem are the introductory teachings, with the destructive words lying upon them, or the representing ranks of Jerusalem, having the capacity to silence those who contradict (Ps 147:2). 'For he has blessed your sons in you,' those who will act and will possess the capacity of thought; for because they become such sons of her, being blessed in her, they never cease to act, having learned to turn to the house of the Lord all the days of their lives. title: The Snow and Mist of Divine Word
english: He brings her children within her, he who sets your borders in peace, with all war having fled from her borders, against the wars that crush, the Lord setting the borders of the city in peace. By saying peace, he imparts to her spiritual food.

And if you wish to say that the educational words of God are fire (not that they are [something] by which one is filled?), you do not err. For it is said in the prophet, in the face of God toward the false prophets, 'What is chaff with grain?' Thus are my words, says the Lord; the words of himself are indeed grain, but theirs are chaff through the word. Just as the wisdom from God is not earthly, nor psychic, nor demonic, but descending from above Him, so also His word, not being from the earth, is sent into the earth, becoming for each of those able to serve Him the same thing as the word given by the Lord to those preaching the gospel with much power. If this thing given, being distributed, runs swiftly to more souls, the word of God, being fulfilled, 'Their voice has gone out into all the earth and their words to the ends of the inhabited world' (Ps 147:4). Truly his taking up has happened, and immediately the evangelical word passed through all the earth, to everyone under the heaven.

Regarding the things said before, it appears to us that these things have been set forth in a parabolic manner, by placing the works of the cosmic creation alongside the economy concerning the church by way of likeness. For just as snow is a layer covering a place, and after this a thaw occurs and water pours out, so the divine word, having dwelt among the Jews first, after this pours out upon all. Therefore also the mission of the word and the blowing of the Spirit are well indicated through the cosmic works: that just as the word comes into the world and the Spirit breathes, the word of the holy and saving teaching went out from Jerusalem to all the inhabited world. If one is to take this also up in allegory, since it stands forth spiritually regarding His running word: for indeed, 'You will wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow' (Ps 51:7), one should not think in terms of sensible snow...

How can the soul be made whiter than snow, which is beyond sensation, if it is not a participant in the brightness of the rational nature through the whiteness of the snow? To this thought the saying, 'If your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow' (Isaiah 1:18), contributes; for one cannot conceive of sins being whitened like physical snow.

Perhaps the most beautiful word cast upon the earth by the Lord is like wool, a garment to be fashioned for the soul, this wool being produced by the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world (John 1:29). Similarly, you will perceive those cast down like crystal flakes and the mist passing like ash. Farmers need snow and mist; for these, when they come upon the offspring, increase them. Just as even upon the good earth of the soul, if the seed has fallen, it is necessary that rain and dew fall, so too snow and mist must come upon our offspring, so that we may bear fruit being nourished by all these.

You will perceive the snow, the crystal, and the mist as temptations brought upon the saints for testing. For they are not being chilled in the love within them by opposing powers, just as 'as a pit cools, so does its wickedness cool' [allusion]. In the face of this cold, who will endure, if not he who, like Peter, Paul, Job, and James the speaker who said 'I became' (James 1:12), is joined with the heat of the day and the frost of the night?

Toward these things you will also take the things said by Moses: 'Let my speech drop as the rain, and my words descend as the dew, as the gentle rain upon the tender grass, and as the snow upon the herb' (Deuteronomy 32:2). For by the word, the sayings of Moses are made like these; by this word, the word sent to the land of God is logically divided into all things spoken. And what is this cold that no one can endure from its presence, to be seen as worthy?
